title: Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence
summary: The first comprehensive US state AI law, imposing duties of reasonable care on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to avoid algorithmic discrimination. Its effective date was delayed from 2026-02-01 to 2026-06-30 by SB 25B-004, enforcement was then suspended by stipulated order in xAI v. Weiser, and it was repealed and reenacted in narrower form by SB 26-189 on 2026-05-14. It never became enforceable.
key_provisions: Repealed and reenacted by SB 26-189 before taking effect

title: Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier AI Models Act
summary: Would have required safety testing and kill switch capabilities for frontier AI models above compute thresholds. Vetoed by Governor Newsom.
key_provisions: Compute threshold triggers ($100M training cost or 10^26 FLOP)
veto_reason: Governor cited concerns about applying strict standards to all AI models regardless of risk context

title: AI Training Data Transparency
summary: Requires developers of generative AI systems to post documentation about training data on their websites.
key_provisions: Applies to GenAI offered in California

title: AI Definition Standardization
summary: Establishes standard definition of artificial intelligence for California law, aligned with NIST and federal definitions.
key_provisions: Standardized AI definition across CA code

title: Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act
summary: First US state law regulating AI in employment. Requires notice and consent before AI is used to analyse video interviews of job applicants, an explanation of how the AI evaluates candidates, limits on sharing the video, and deletion on request.
key_provisions: Notice to candidates before AI analysis

title: Automated Employment Decision Tools
summary: Requires bias audits and notice for automated employment decision tools used in hiring in NYC.

title: AI Advisory Council
summary: Creates advisory council to study AI use in state government and make recommendations.
key_provisions: Study of AI in state government

title: AI Policy Act
summary: Created an AI learning laboratory and disclosure duties for generative AI. Materially amended in 2025 by SB 226, which narrowed the consumer-facing disclosure duty to cases where a consumer asks whether AI is in use, and by SB 332, which extended the Act's repeal date to 2027-07-01.

title: ELVIS Act (AI Voice Protection)
summary: Protects artists from unauthorized AI-generated replicas of their voice and likeness.
key_provisions: Voice and likeness protection from AI

title: AI Inventory and Assessment
summary: Required state agencies to inventory AI systems and conduct impact assessments. Substantially supplemented in 2026 by the Connecticut Artificial Intelligence Responsibility and Transparency Act (Public Act 26-15), which extends AI duties to private employers and other sectors.

title: Automated Decision-Making Technology in Consequential Decisions
summary: Repeals and reenacts the Colorado AI Act in narrower form. Replaces the risk-management regime for high-risk AI with a notice-and-transparency framework governing automated decision-making technology that materially influences a consequential decision.
key_provisions: Drops risk management programs and annual impact assessments
Pre-use notice before covered technology materially influences a consequential decision
Right to correct inaccurate data and request meaningful human review
Developer duty to supply deployers with technical documentation
Attorney General exclusive enforcement with required rulemaking

title: Illinois Human Rights Act Amendment on Artificial Intelligence
summary: Amends the Illinois Human Rights Act to make it a civil rights violation for an employer to use AI that discriminates on the basis of a protected class in employment decisions. Enacted as Public Act 103-0804 and effective 2026-01-01.
key_provisions: Bars AI that has a discriminatory effect in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discipline and discharge
Bars use of ZIP code as a proxy for a protected class
Requires notice to applicants and employees when AI is used
Enforced by the Illinois Department of Human Rights

title: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
summary: First US state frontier AI safety law, enacted after the veto of SB 1047. Requires large frontier developers to publish safety frameworks and transparency reports and to report critical safety incidents to the state.
key_provisions: Publish a frontier AI framework describing catastrophic-risk mitigations
Publish a transparency report at or before deployment of a new frontier model
Report critical safety incidents to Cal OES within 15 days, or 24 hours if imminent danger
Whistleblower protections and an anonymous internal reporting channel
Civil penalties up to USD 1 million per violation, enforced by the Attorney General
Creates the CalCompute public computing consortium

title: Companion Chatbot Safeguards
summary: Regulates companion chatbots. Requires disclosure that the user is interacting with AI, recurring reminders for minors, and protocols for responding to expressions of self-harm.
key_provisions: Clear disclosure that the user is interacting with an AI system
Crisis and self-harm response protocols with referral to crisis services
Prohibition on sexually explicit content with known minors

title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA)
summary: Third US state comprehensive AI law, built on intent rather than risk tiers. Prohibits specified harmful AI uses, constrains government use of AI, and creates a regulatory sandbox. Disparate impact alone does not establish a violation.
key_provisions: Prohibits developing or deploying AI with intent to incite self-harm or crime, or to discriminate unlawfully
Prohibits AI producing unlawful sexual deepfakes or child sexual abuse material
Bars government social scoring and biometric identification from public data without consent
Requires health care providers to disclose AI use in diagnosis or treatment
36-month regulatory sandbox administered by the Department of Information Resources
Attorney General exclusive enforcement with a 60-day cure period and no private right of action

title: Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act
summary: Second US state frontier model safety law after California SB 53. Requires large frontier developers to publish safety protocols and to report safety incidents to the state.
key_provisions: Large frontier developers must write and publish safety protocols
Safety incident reporting to the state within 72 hours
Creates an AI oversight function with rulemaking and annual public reporting

title: Connecticut Artificial Intelligence Responsibility and Transparency Act (CART Act)
summary: Enacted as Public Act 26-15, one of the most comprehensive US state AI laws. Covers automated employment decisions, AI companions, frontier model safety, content provenance and online platforms used by minors, with obligations staggered from 2026-10-01 into 2028.
key_provisions: Written notice before automated tools drive major employment decisions
Disclosure to the Department of Labor when a covered workforce reduction relates to AI use
Companion chatbot disclosure and crisis-intervention duties
